```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Grim Trigger compares the profit from continued coordination with one period of
defection followed by Bertrand punishment forever. This is a sustainability
condition under a specified repeated game, not evidence that coordination
actually occurs. Use **coordination 0.1.0** and compatible **antitrust >= 0.99.43**.
Prices are currency per unit; inside size is units sold per period.

## Reuse a Bertrand model

Firm A owns products 1 and 2 before the merger. Afterwards B also owns product 4.
The coalition indices `c(1,3)` select products associated with two distinct
firms, and the IC comparison includes every product in those firms' portfolios.

```{r grim-fit}
library(antitrust)
library(coordination)
fit <- antitrust::logit(
  prices = c(10, 12, 11, 9), shares = c(.25, .20, .18, .17),
  margins = c(.40, .38, .35, .25),
  ownerPre = c("A", "A", "B", "C"),
  ownerPost = c("A", "A", "B", "B"), insideSize = 1000
)
result <- calcProducerSurplusGrimTrigger(fit, coalition = c(1, 3),
  discount = rep(.8, 4), preMerger = TRUE)
knitr::kable(result, digits = 3)
```

`Coord`, `Defect` and `Punish` are single-period producer surplus in currency.
`Discount` is a factor strictly between zero and one, not an interest rate.
All products of a participating firm need valid factors, including product 2
although it was not listed as a coalition index. `IC` is a firm-portfolio
comparison repeated on that firm's product rows, not an independent product
decision. `Coalition` marks membership and should not be summed as a profit.

## Aggregate portfolios and change patience

For a common factor delta within a firm, compare
`C/(1-delta)` with `D + delta*P/(1-delta)`, where C, D and P sum **all** its
product profits. A higher factor gives future punishment more weight. The next
small sensitivity reuses the existing fitted object and changes only the
specified discount and ownership state selected by `preMerger`.

```{r grim-sensitivity}
firm_ids <- list(pre = c("A", "A", "B", "C"),
                 post = c("A", "A", "B", "B"))
portfolio_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(TRUE, FALSE), function(pre) {
  state <- if (pre) "pre" else "post"
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c(.05, .8), function(delta) {
    out <- calcProducerSurplusGrimTrigger(fit, coalition = c(1, 3),
      discount = rep(delta, 4), preMerger = pre)
    firms <- firm_ids[[state]][match(rownames(out), fit@labels)]
    do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(firms), function(firm) {
      rows <- firms == firm
      C <- sum(out$Coord[rows]); D <- sum(out$Defect[rows])
      P <- sum(out$Punish[rows])
      data.frame(state = state, firm = firm, discount = delta,
        coord = C, defect = D, punish = P,
        repeated_game_gain = C/(1-delta) - D - delta*P/(1-delta),
        IC = all(out$IC[rows]))
    }))
  }))
}))
knitr::kable(portfolio_results, digits = 3)
```

Read `repeated_game_gain` in discounted currency. Positive values favor
continued coordination. Compare the low/high discount rows within a state;
then compare the pre/post rows for a given firm and discount. A post-merger
portfolio can include an additional product, so comparisons must preserve the
correct ownership state. These illustrative values are safely away from an
exact indifference boundary.

```{r portfolio-check, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(all(portfolio_results$IC ==
                (portfolio_results$repeated_game_gain > 0)),
          any(!portfolio_results$IC[portfolio_results$discount == .05]),
          all(portfolio_results$IC[portfolio_results$discount == .8]))
```

## Calibration assumptions and limitations

The main workflow uses `isCollusion = FALSE`, which preserves demand/cost
parameters calibrated from ordinary baseline ownership. Setting
`isCollusion = TRUE` **recalibrates demand and cost** under an assumed baseline
coalition; it is not an output-format switch. Do not toggle it merely to obtain
an additional table.

The simplified portfolio inequality above assumes a common factor within each
firm. The API allows product-specific inputs; that general case must be
interpreted using its actual discounted portfolio calculation. The current code
uses a strict comparison in the pre state and a weak comparison in the post
state at exact equality. This guide avoids equality and does not change that
existing behavior.

The method dispatches on compatible antitrust Bertrand models, including several
demand subclasses. Compatibility does not establish empirical adequacy or a
unique collusive outcome. See `?calcProducerSurplusGrimTrigger` for the full
contract, the [PLE identification guide](price-leadership.html) ([source](https://github.com/luciu5/coordination/blob/main/vignettes/price-leadership.Rmd)) for a different
calibration question, and the
[model reference](https://github.com/luciu5/coordination/blob/main/doc/coordination-model-reference.md)
for the longer repeated-game discussion.
